chunks: I found in some books that Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from al-Mufaḍḍal [al-Fuḍayl], who said:

If someone recites “Innā Anzalnāh” seven times next to the grave of a believer, Allāh will send an angel to that grave who will worship Allāh next to it. The rewards for this worship will be registered for the one who is dead and (also) for him (the person who came to visit the grave of the believer).

When this believer will be resurrected, he will not undergo any terror without Allāh removing it from him through the angel who was dedicated to his grave, and he will enter Paradise in the company of that angel.

He added, “(When you go to the graves of the believers), recite (the chapter of) Al-Ḥamd one time, (the chapter of) Innā Anzalnāh seven times, then recite the Mu’awwadhatayn, (the chapter of) Qul Huwallāhu Aḥad, and Ayatul Kursī, each three times.”

key_terms.آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ: Ayat al-Kursi (The Verse of the Throne)
key_terms.إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ: Innā Anzalnāh (Surah Ad-Dukhan, verse 3), a specific Quranic verse mentioned for its merit.
key_terms.الْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ: The two Surahs of protection (Al-Falaq and An-Nas)
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: Glory be to Allah (part of Mu'awwadhatayn)

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards of reciting Quran at the grave of a believer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the intercessory power of Quranic recitation in the afterlife, a key concept in Shia piety regarding the state of the soul in the grave (*Barzakh*). The text specifies a ritual where reciting Surah Ad-Dukhan seven times, accompanied by Surah Al-Fatiha, the Mu'awwidhatayn, Surah Al-Ikhlas, and Ayat al-Kursi, invokes a dedicated angel who shields the deceased from the trials of resurrection (*Hawl*) and ensures entry into Paradise.
